reason: The cited evidence does not directly support the specific mechanism linking Mo reduction to enhanced dislocation mobility or the quantitative predictions. E3 notes Mo increases room-temperature strength and Nb increases ductility, but does not address the effect of partial Mo/Nb substitution on plasticity or strength retention in the NbZrTiHfMo system. E1 and E2 only confirm BCC phase stability in related alloys, not the proposed composition or property changes.
premises: Reducing Mo content in BCC RHEAs lowers electronegativity difference and lattice distortion, enhancing dislocation mobility and plasticity.
Increasing Nb content in BCC RHEAs promotes ductility and dislocation motion without severely reducing solid-solution strengthening.
Partial substitution of Mo by Nb preserves a disordered BCC solid solution phase.
A 20–30% Mo reduction maintains yield strength within 10% of the baseline while increasing compressive fracture strain by ~50%.
